level00.imageAlt: Archaeological excavation camp in an ancient marshland
level00.captionInitial: You have arrived at the excavation camp.
level00.title: Tartessos Quest
level00.paragraph1: An archaeological expedition has discovered a sealed entrance beneath the southern sands. The first clues point to a forgotten chamber of ancient Tartessos.
level00.paragraph2: No one knows what lies beyond the threshold. The inscriptions found so far have not yet been translated; the ancient Tartessian language remains a mystery.
level00.paragraph3: Your mission is to accompany the expedition, decipher its signs, and advance step by step toward the heart of a lost civilization.
level00.paragraph4: Each chamber will reveal part of the mystery. Each decision will bring the expedition closer to the truth Tartessos left buried.
level00.successParagraph2: The expedition can begin the descent toward the first Tartessian threshold.
level00.hint: Next mission: proceed to the expedition registry.

level01.captionInitial: The expedition’s first registry awaits you on the campaign table.
level01.captionCompleted: You have been registered as a member of the expedition.
level01.title: ADVENTURER NAME
level01.paragraph1: Before crossing the threshold, the expedition must record the names of those who will descend into the sealed chambers.
level01.paragraph2: The registry lies open on a table covered with maps, compasses, and ceramic fragments marked with ancient signs.
level01.paragraph3: Once your name has been entered, the expedition guide will give the signal to continue toward the main entrance.
level01.helpIntro: To complete this exercise, you must modify a class parameter in ObjectScript and compile the class.
level01.helpStep3: Replace the value CHANGE_ME with your name.
level01.helpStep4: Compile the class from VS Code or from the IRIS terminal.
level01.helpStep5: Press SUBMIT FORM to run the validation.
level01.helpExpectedText: The GetAdventurerName method must return your name and store it in the ^adventurerName global.
level01.successMessage: The form has been received successfully.
level01.genericValidationError: The form could not be validated.
level01.connectionError: Could not contact the registration post.
level01.formNotCompletedError: The form has not been completed.

level02.captionInitial: The campaign cabinet holds the expedition’s basic equipment.
level02.title: THE EXCAVATION KIT
level02.paragraph1: Before entering the work area, the foreman points to an old wooden cabinet reinforced with iron.
level02.paragraph2: Its shelves hold tools worn by previous campaigns: dust-covered hats, flashlights, boxes of batteries, and excavation instruments.
level02.paragraph3: Nothing must be missing before leaving camp. The expedition will only move forward once the equipment has been checked.
level02.helpIntro: To complete this exercise, you must implement a class method that prepares tools using conditions and loops.
level02.helpStep2: Find the PrepareTool(tool As %String, total As %Integer) method.
level02.helpStep3: Check the value of tool using If statements.
level02.helpStep4: For each valid tool, create a For loop from 1 to total.
level02.helpStep5: Inside each loop, call the corresponding method from Tartessos.Quest.ExcavationKitUtils.
level02.helpStep6: Use AddTrowel(), AddHat(), AddFlashlight(), or AddBattery() as appropriate.
level02.helpStep7: Return 1 if the tool is valid and 0 if it is not. Compile the class before reviewing the kit.
level02.helpExpectedText: The validation will call PrepareTool with a test value and check that each tool global contains the expected quantity.
level02.genericValidationError: The equipment is not ready yet.
level02.connectionError: Could not contact the tool station.

level03.imageAlt: Underground passage with access to several chambers and a central collapse
level03.captionInitial: The first passage of the hypogeum branches into chambers that have not yet been classified.
level03.captionCompleted: The initial chamber map has been organized.
level03.title: DISCOVERING THE CHAMBERS
level03.paragraph1: The descent leads into a stone passage. Dark entrances open on both sides, while a collapse blocks the central path.
level03.paragraph2: The marks on the walls suggest that not every chamber served the same purpose. Some look like corridors, others like gathering halls, burial spaces, or sealed storage rooms.
level03.paragraph3: Before moving forward, the expedition must organize the first map of the ruins and classify each type of chamber.
level03.helpTitle: How to define the chamber model
level03.helpIntro: To complete this exercise, you must create a set of ObjectScript classes using packages, inheritance, and typed properties.
level03.helpStep3: Make Chamber extend %RegisteredObject and mark it as Abstract.
level03.helpStep4: Add the Code, Name, Description, Level, and IsSealed properties to Chamber.
level03.helpStep5: Create the Corridor, Hall, Mortuary, and Storage classes in the same package.
level03.helpStep6: Make all specific classes extend Tartessos.Quest.Chambers.Chamber.
level03.helpStep7: Add the Length and HasFork properties to Corridor.
level03.helpStep8: Add the specific properties for Hall, Mortuary, and Storage according to the exercise statement.
level03.helpStep9: Compile the Tartessos.Quest.Chambers package and press REVIEW CHAMBERS.
level03.helpExpectedText: The validation will check that the classes exist, that inheritance is correct, and that the properties have the expected types and initial values.
level03.successMessage: The first chamber model has been recognized.
level03.genericValidationError: Not all chamber types have been recognized.
level03.connectionError: Could not contact the excavation chief.
level03.recognizedChambersIntro: The following chamber types have been identified at the site:

level04.imageAlt: Open field notebook with a chamber sketch and handwritten notes
level04.captionInitial: The field notebook awaits the expedition’s first entries.
level04.captionCompleted: The first notebook lines have been recognized.
level04.title: THE FIELD NOTEBOOK
level04.paragraph1: After classifying the first chambers, the expedition opens a field notebook on the work table.
level04.paragraph2: Each discovered room must be recorded in the right place, without confusing corridors, halls, mortuary chambers, or storage rooms.
level04.paragraph3: Once the first notes are ready, the expedition chief will check whether the notebook can accompany the descent.
level04.helpIntro: To complete this exercise, you must create an ObjectScript class with list properties, an instance method, and a class method.
level04.helpStep8: GetTotalLines() must return the sum of all elements in all lists.
level04.helpStep10: GetChamberType() must return Hall, Mortuary, Storage, or Corridor depending on the received type.
level04.helpStep12: From the terminal, create a Notebook instance, create a Hall instance, and add it to the hall list.
level04.helpStep13: Store the result of GetTotalLines() in ^notebook("totalLines") and the result of GetChamberType(myHall) in ^notebook("firstChamberType").
level04.helpExpectedText: The validation will check that the ^notebook global exists and then create a Notebook instance and a Hall instance to verify the methods.
level04.successMessage: The first notebook entries have been recognized.
level04.notebookIntro: The notebook contains the first valid marks of the expedition:
level04.genericValidationError: The field notebook is not complete yet.
level04.connectionError: Could not contact the note station.

level05.imageAlt: Field notebook in the explorer’s hands with verified notes
level05.captionInitial: We must ensure that the chambers are correctly registered.
level05.captionCompleted: The chambers have been incorporated into the site record.
level05.title: THE CHAMBER REGISTRY
level05.paragraph1: Our field notebook is ready and we have included the first notes; we must make sure to document everything we discover.
level05.paragraph2: Each chamber must be registered to document the progress through the hypogeum. Documentation is essential for presenting the findings to the public.
level05.paragraph3: Before continuing, we must ensure that no detail about the discovered chambers is lost.
level05.helpIntro: To complete this exercise, you must convert the chamber model into a persistent model and create a utility that validates, classifies, and saves each chamber.
level05.helpStep3: Keep Chamber as an Abstract class.
level05.helpStep4: Add the IsRelevant As %Boolean property with initial value 0.
level05.helpStep5: Check that Corridor, Hall, Mortuary, and Storage still extend Tartessos.Quest.Chambers.Chamber.
level05.helpStep6: Create or complete the Tartessos.Quest.ExcavationUtils class.
level05.helpStep7: Implement the addPage(chamber As Tartessos.Quest.Chambers.Chamber) As %Status method.
level05.helpStep8: Validate that chamber is a valid object.
level05.helpStep9: Validate that the required fields are filled in.
level05.helpStep10: Check whether chamber is Hall, Mortuary, Storage, or Corridor.
level05.helpStep11: Mark Hall as relevant if HasMosaic is 1.
level05.helpStep12: Mark Mortuary as relevant if TombCount is greater than 1.
level05.helpStep13: Mark Storage as relevant if ContainsSupplies is 1.
level05.helpStep14: Leave Corridor as not relevant by default and save the chamber with %Save().
level05.helpStep15: Compile the classes and press REVIEW REGISTRY.
level05.helpExpectedText: The validation will check that the chambers are persistent, that IsRelevant is calculated correctly, and that the objects can be saved and opened from IRIS.
level05.successMessage: The chambers have been documented correctly.
level05.registryIntro: The registry recognizes the relevance of the discovered chambers:

level05.connectionError: Could not contact the excavation registry.

level06.imageAlt: Mortuary chamber with an inscribed sarcophagus, pottery, offerings, and an ancient sword
level06.captionInitial: The mortuary chamber preserves finds that must be linked with care.
level06.captionCompleted: The sarcophagi and offerings have been linked correctly.
level06.title: THE MORTUARY CHAMBER
level06.paragraph1: The expedition enters a silent chamber. At its center rests a stone sarcophagus covered by an inscription that may reveal who once owned such a majestic tomb.
level06.paragraph2: Around it lie ceramics, Greek vessels, and offerings that speak of ancient exchanges with Punic peoples and Mediterranean traders.
level06.paragraph3: Among the remains also lies a carp’s tongue sword from the Bronze Age. Every find must be examined in detail before leaving the chamber.
level06.helpTitle: How to connect sarcophagi and offerings
level06.helpIntro: To complete this exercise, you must create a connected model with relationships, validations, and indexes.
level06.helpStep2: Add a Sarcophagi relationship to Tartessos.Quest.Finds.Sarcophagus.
level06.helpStep4: Add the Owner, StateConservation, Material, and Inscriptions properties to Sarcophagus.
level06.helpStep5: Add the Mortuary relationship from Sarcophagus to Tartessos.Quest.Chambers.Mortuary.
level06.helpStep6: Add the Offerings relationship from Sarcophagus to Tartessos.Quest.Finds.Offering.
level06.helpStep8: Add the Material, Classification, Description, and Inscription properties to Offering.
level06.helpStep9: Add the Sarcophagus relationship from Offering to Tartessos.Quest.Finds.Sarcophagus.
level06.helpStep10: Use VALUELIST on properties with closed sets of values.
level06.helpStep11: Add an index on Classification in Offering.
level06.helpStep14: Compile the classes and press REVIEW FINDS.
level06.helpExpectedText: The validation will check that Mortuary, Sarcophagus, and Offering are related, that the Classification index exists, and that validations reject incorrect data.
level06.successMessage: The sarcophagus and its offerings have been correctly documented.
level06.findsIntro: The chamber now shows a coherent structure of finds:
